articleTitle: Managing the challenge of cognitive radio
publicationTitle: IET Seminar on Cognitive Radio Communications: European Activities and Progress
abstract: The paper presents the evolution trends and challenges of cognitive radio as well as the radio RF circuits. Cognitive radio challenges are unconventional and interdisciplinary in nature ( RF, analog, digital, signal processing etc.). Spectrum access condition based on different technique: sensing technique/geo-location/beacon involves RF design, robust signal processing, pattern recognition. Cognitive radio transmit spectrum is very challenging and need to combine different techniques. Consider reducing output power to relax ACLR and allow aggregation.

articleTitle: Eigenvalue-based spectrum sensing for cognitive radio
publicationTitle: IET Seminar on Cognitive Radio Communications: European Activities and Progress
abstract: We studied the distributions of the ratio of the extreme eigenvalues and maximum eigenvalue of the complex Wishart matrix. We derived the exact decision thresholds as a function of the desired probability of false alarm for MME and MED based cooperative spectrum sensing, which are able to handle for both correlated and uncorrelated Gaussian noise samples. The expression for the decision threshold was simplified for two receiving antenna or for the case of two user collaborative sensing. We also derived a simpler closed-form threshold function using an asymptotic distribution with equal numbers of receive antennas and signal samples, that is m = n and large n. We shown that analytical and empirical results are coincide with each other. The probability of detection performance using the proposed exact decision thresholds achieve significant performance gains compared to the performance using the asymptotic decision threshold reported in the literature, which leads to efficient spectrum usage.
